subtitle: One Blackhole chip (qb2, p300 board, chips 0 and 2, AICLK 1300-1350 MHz during runs). Seconds from process start until the first result is ready. Median of 1-2 runs (chip time ran out).
footer: tt-bio main at d54465839 + perf/startup harness (branch wk/startup-time-report) | ttnn 0.68.0 | host tt-quietbox2, Ryzen 7 9700X 16 threads, load 7-13 from other jobs | weights on local NVMe | 2026-11-20
method:
What a bar is. One fresh Python process per run, through the same entry points JapanFold serving uses (perf/spd/bench.py -> worker predict_one; perf/bmk/design_cell.py for RFD4; load_esmc + embed_sequences for ESMC). A sitecustomize tracer (perf/startup/trace) wraps, from outside the model code, imports of torch/ttnn/tt_bio, device open, checkpoint check, weight reads (torch.load, safetensors), host->device tensor creation (ttnn.from_torch/as_tensor/to_device), trace capture, model load and each prediction, and charges every interval of the main thread to the innermost one. Time no wrap claims is split by a 20 ms stack sampler.
Cold vs warm. Cold = empty private TT_METAL_CACHE, so every kernel JIT-compiles. Warm = a second process on the cache the cold run just filled. Kernel compile = cold total - warm total, the only difference between the two runs. Serving keeps its kernel cache across restarts (cleared only on an SFPI change), so users normally see the warm number.
Disk. The page cache of every weight file was dropped (posix_fadvise DONTNEED) before each run, so weights come from NVMe; Python packages stay in page cache. Round 2 where it ran, else round 1; ESMC uses rounds 2-3. The disk read is at most 5 s in every run, so round choice barely moves a bar. Chip time ran out before the planned 3 rounds.
Inputs. ESMFold2, Boltz-2: c730 (730-token SPD cell input). Protenix-v2, OpenDDE, OpenFold3: l512 (512 aa), because c730 crashes all three on this main with an L1 circular-buffer clash (reported to SPD). RFD4: its S336 design cell. BindCraft 2: PD-L1 example, 80-aa binder, one trajectory = one result. ESMC-300M: the c730 sequence. Normal mode, not --fast.
Caveats. JIT compile is CPU-bound and the host ran other jobs (load 7-13 of 16 threads), so cold compile is likely longer than on an idle host. Clock sampled every second during each run. OpenFold3: its warm-cache run crashes (L1 clash, reported to SPD), so its bar is one cold run with compile inside the other phases. BindCraft 2: one trajectory runs 100-450 s depending on its seed, which swamps compile, so its bar is the cold run as measured. WH not measured: no Wormhole chip was free under the allocation rules without touching JapanFold users.
